skill.name: site-architecture
skill.description: Plans website page hierarchies, navigation, URL structures, visual sitemaps, and internal linking for clear user journeys and search visibility.
skill.summary: Create practical website architecture plans with page trees, URL maps, navigation specifications, and internal linking guidance.

content.value_statement: Unstructured websites make pages difficult to find and maintain. This skill creates page hierarchies, navigation plans, URL maps, and internal linking recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Creates complete page hierarchies as readable ASCII trees.
Produces visual sitemap specifications using Mermaid diagrams.
Maps pages to consistent, descriptive URL patterns.
Defines header, footer, sidebar, and breadcrumb navigation.
Plans hub-and-spoke and cross-section internal links.
Adapts templates for SaaS, content, commerce, documentation, hybrid, and local sites.
limitations: Does not create or repair XML sitemaps.
Does not crawl websites or verify live links.
Requires a content inventory for accurate restructuring plans.
Provides architecture guidance, not implementation in a content management system.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Site
use_cases.description: Define pages, navigation, URLs, and internal links before design and development begin.

use_cases.title: Restructure a Growing Website
use_cases.description: Group existing pages, reduce navigation complexity, and identify redirects for moved content.

use_cases.title: Organize Documentation
use_cases.description: Create section hierarchies, sidebar navigation, breadcrumbs, and predictable documentation URLs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Page Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the site architecture for a [site type]. Include pages for [business needs] and serve [primary audiences]. Provide a page hierarchy and URL map.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new website

prompt_templates.title: Design Website Navigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design header, footer, mobile, and breadcrumb navigation for this page list: [pages]. Prioritize [business goals] and explain each navigation placement.

prompt_templates.title: Restructure an Existing Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Reorganize this content inventory: [pages and URLs]. Preserve [important URLs], identify redirects, reduce depth, and provide before-and-after hierarchies.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Scalable Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design architecture for [site] with [number] templated pages across [sections]. Include hubs, URL rules, navigation exposure, internal links, and orphan-page controls.

output_examples.input: Plan a small SaaS website with features, pricing, customer stories, resources, and documentation.
output: Primary navigation: Features, Pricing, Customers, Resources, and Docs.
Core hierarchy: Homepage, section hubs, detail pages, company pages, and legal pages.
Internal links connect feature pages with customer stories, documentation, and pricing.

output_examples.input: Reorganize a content site with many uncategorized articles and hidden guides.
output: Create topic hubs for major audiences and move related articles beneath each hub.
Add Guides to primary navigation and expose secondary topics through hub pages.
Map every changed URL to a permanent redirect and preserve strong existing URLs.
Link each article to its topic hub and relevant guides.

output_examples.input: Add integration and comparison pages without crowding the main navigation.
output: Create /integrations and /compare hubs linked from relevant product and resource pages.
Use consistent detail paths such as /integrations/name and /compare/name.
List selected integrations in product navigation and place complete directories on each hub.
Connect comparison pages to features, pricing, and customer evidence.

best_practices: Provide business goals, audiences, site type, and important pages before planning.
Share the current URL inventory when restructuring an existing website.
Review page priorities and navigation labels with user research or analytics.
anti_patterns: Do not change established URLs without a complete redirect map.
Do not place every page in the primary navigation.
Do not treat visual hierarchy as a substitute for content inventory.

faq.question: Does this skill create XML sitemaps?
faq.answer: No. It plans human-facing page hierarchy and navigation. Use a technical SEO workflow for XML sitemap generation and validation.

faq.question: Can it restructure an existing website?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current page inventory, URLs, performance priorities, and known navigation problems.

faq.question: What output formats are supported?
faq.answer: It can provide ASCII page trees, Mermaid sitemap specifications, URL tables, navigation plans, and internal linking recommendations.

faq.question: Does it inspect a live website?
faq.answer: No. It uses information and inventories supplied in the conversation or available project context.

faq.question: Which site types can it plan?
faq.answer: It includes patterns for SaaS, content, commerce, documentation, hybrid, and small business websites.

faq.question: How should existing URLs be handled?
faq.answer: Preserve valuable URLs when possible. Create permanent redirects for every moved page and verify them during implementation.
